title: Function Calling is All You Need — Full Workshop, with Ilan Bigio of OpenAI
talk_summary: A live-coding workshop showing that agents, memory, RAG, delegation, and async task management are all just loops around function calling, implemented from scratch in ~70 lines rather than via frameworks. It also covers tool-count scaling (10-20 tools per agent, triage/handoff routing for more), async task IDs with polling, and a self-writing-tool demo.

takeaways.technique: Triage agent + handoff routing instead of one giant tool list
takeaways.what_they_do: When tool count grows, split functions into clusters behind sub-agents and give a triage agent only 'transfer_to_X' functions; the triage agent routes, then the sub-agent calls the real function.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the primary use case for agents and handoffs is just a glorified triage through uh multiple functions
takeaways.numbers: reliable tool library ~10-20 per agent; 120 functions only worked with fine-tuning on GPT-3.5

takeaways.technique: Async task IDs with create_task/check_task polling
takeaways.what_they_do: Long delegations return immediately with a task ID ('response pending'); the model keeps conversing and later calls check_task to poll status, instead of blocking the turn.
takeaways.evidence_quote: return delegated, right? response pending. Um and then later I can say like you know check tasks

takeaways.technique: Parallel tool execution with serialized result application
takeaways.what_they_do: Run independent tool calls concurrently via async, but push results through a single message queue so generations on the same history never interleave.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we want work to happen at the same time but we don't want um like multiple generations to happen with the same history
takeaways.numbers: 5 sequential 1s sleeps took >5s; async version returned in ~1s

takeaways.what_they_do: Before storing a memory, retrieve semantically similar ones and have a model check for contradiction; link old→new with a timestamped pointer so retrieval can surface only the latest or the full chain.
takeaways.evidence_quote: when you are about to store memory do a retrieval like do search to find similar memories ... and then do an explicit check

takeaways.technique: Dynamic function loading / two-step tool call
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of passing all tools, load only the relevant subset based on input via embeddings or a first routing call; the speaker notes this converges with handoffs.

takeaways.technique: Self-writing tools via eval — explicitly unsafe
takeaways.what_they_do: Agent generates Python source for a new tool, evals it, and appends it to its own tool list; speaker repeatedly flags it as dangerous.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I'm going to do something very unsafe ... eval of Python. Don't do this. Don't do this, kids
